title: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: Cycle, Symptom and Fertility Management

evidenceAudit.scope: Woman or adolescent in primary care, a gynaecology or an endocrine clinic in Saudi Arabia with suspected or confirmed polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS): diagnosis by the 2023 international guideline criteria, screening for glucose, lipid, blood pressure, sleep and mood problems, lifestyle care, management of irregular cycles and hirsutism, metabolic treatment with metformin, ovulation induction and pregnancy planning. Uses the 2023 International Evidence-based Guideline (the Saudi-relevant prevalence comes from a 2026 Gulf Cooperation Council meta-analysis), with doses, dilution, administration and contraindications taken from product labels.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-20.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: No Saudi or Saudi Ministry of Health PCOS guideline was found; the clinical source is the 2023 International Evidence-based Guideline and the authority is shown as Other. The Saudi prevalence figure is from a 2026 Gulf Cooperation Council systematic review that uses the newer name polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS).
The guideline recommends drug classes but gives few doses; all doses, administration and contraindications come from the product label named in each row.

The 2023 guideline treats most PCOS drugs as off-label (combined pill for hirsutism and cycles, metformin, letrozole, clomiphene, spironolactone): explain this to the patient and confirm the local formulary.

Letrozole: the label is for breast cancer (2.5 mg once daily); the guideline gives no ovulation-induction dose. The start dose 2.5 mg on cycle days 3 to 7 comes from a 2023 to 2024 randomised trial (PMC10811237), not from a guideline; confirm with the fertility service. Dose escalation steps are not given.

Spironolactone dose 25 to 100 mg a day is from the guideline practice point (Section 4.6.5); the US label covers heart failure, hypertension and oedema only, so its dose, administration and contraindications are used for safety.
Medroxyprogesterone acetate cycle length and interval for PCOS are not set by the guideline; the label doses for secondary amenorrhoea are shown and the interval is a prescriber decision.

The combined pill shown is a levonorgestrel 150 microgram plus ethinylestradiol 30 microgram 28-day pack because the guideline names no preferred product (Recommendation 4.2.4); the Saudi marketed products were not checked.
Gonadotrophins, laparoscopic ovarian drilling, in vitro fertilisation and bariatric surgery are named in the guideline but are specialist care and are not written as regimens.

Inositol and anti-obesity drugs (liraglutide, semaglutide, orlistat) are recognised in the guideline but are not written as regimens because they are not first-line for PCOS and no dose was taken from a label.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; the guideline asks laboratories to use their own assay-specific ranges for testosterone and anti-Mullerian hormone.
Differentials follow standard clinical practice and the guideline exclusion list but were not drawn from one source section.
Figures were read through automated extraction of the open-access journal XML and DailyMed label XML; spot-check each dose against the source during clinical review.
Menopause, bariatric surgery and paediatric endocrine care are outside the scope of this primary-care and referral topic and are only mentioned briefly.
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register returned an empty page from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.

pathophysiology.summary: PCOS is a common hormone condition of women of reproductive age with high male-type hormones (androgens), missed or rare ovulation and many small follicles in the ovaries; the 2018 and 2023 guideline calls it a lifelong condition (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.7.1). Insulin resistance is part of the condition and pushes the ovary to make more androgen; routine insulin tests are not accurate enough to use in care (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.9.12). A 2026 pooled analysis of 24 Gulf Cooperation Council studies, mostly Saudi, found a prevalence of 17.6% (95% confidence interval 13.0% to 23.4%) with very high variation between studies because they used different criteria; the global figure by Rotterdam criteria is 10% to 13% (GCC meta-analysis 2026, Results; International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.6.1). Women with PCOS have more impaired glucose tolerance, type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular risk factors, obstructive sleep apnoea, depression, anxiety and endometrial cancer risk, whatever their weight (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendations 1.8 to 1.11 and 2.2). Pregnancy carries more miscarriage, gestational diabetes, hypertension in pregnancy, preterm birth and caesarean section, so PCOS should be flagged in antenatal care (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 4.10.1 and 4.10.2). Without regular periods the lining of the womb is not shed, so the risk of endometrial hyperplasia rises; cycle control and progestogen protect the lining (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendations 1.11.1 and 1.11.4).
keyMechanisms: PCOS is a common hormone condition of women of reproductive age with high male-type hormones (androgens), missed or rare ovulation and many small follicles in the ovaries; the 2018 and 2023 guideline calls it a lifelong condition (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.7.1).

Insulin resistance is part of the condition and pushes the ovary to make more androgen; routine insulin tests are not accurate enough to use in care (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.9.12).

A 2026 pooled analysis of 24 Gulf Cooperation Council studies, mostly Saudi, found a prevalence of 17.6% (95% confidence interval 13.0% to 23.4%) with very high variation between studies because they used different criteria; the global figure by Rotterdam criteria is 10% to 13% (GCC meta-analysis 2026, Results; International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.6.1).

Women with PCOS have more impaired glucose tolerance, type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular risk factors, obstructive sleep apnoea, depression, anxiety and endometrial cancer risk, whatever their weight (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendations 1.8 to 1.11 and 2.2).

Pregnancy carries more miscarriage, gestational diabetes, hypertension in pregnancy, preterm birth and caesarean section, so PCOS should be flagged in antenatal care (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 4.10.1 and 4.10.2).

Without regular periods the lining of the womb is not shed, so the risk of endometrial hyperplasia rises; cycle control and progestogen protect the lining (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendations 1.11.1 and 1.11.4).

symptoms: Irregular, infrequent or absent periods (cycles shorter than 21 days or longer than 35 days, or fewer than 8 a year in adults) (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.1.1).
Excess facial or body hair, acne and scalp hair thinning (International PCOS guideline 2023, Section 1.3).
Difficulty becoming pregnant; weight gain; low mood, anxiety and poor body image (International PCOS guideline 2023, Sections 2 and 5).
Snoring with unrefreshing sleep, daytime tiredness (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.10.2).
physicalSigns: Hirsutism on the modified Ferriman-Gallwey score of 4 to 6 or more depending on ethnicity (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.3.5).
Acne, female pattern hair loss, acanthosis nigricans (clinical judgment).
Raised body mass index and waist; blood pressure measured at every visit (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.8.4).
redFlags: Rapidly progressive or severe hirsutism, voice deepening or very high testosterone: look for an ovarian or adrenal tumour or non-classical adrenal hyperplasia (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.2.9).

Amenorrhoea of more than three months or heavy unexplained bleeding with a thick endometrium: assess for endometrial hyperplasia with ultrasound and biopsy (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.11.5).
Moderate or severe depression, anxiety or self-harm thoughts: assess and refer the same day (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 2.2.3).

Positive pregnancy test before any ovulation drug, letrozole, clomiphene or spironolactone: stop and arrange antenatal care (letrozole and clomiphene labels, Section 4; International PCOS guideline 2023, Section 5).
Woman with PCOS who is pregnant: early glucose test and blood pressure plan; screen for gestational diabetes at 24 to 28 weeks (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 4.10.7).
precipitants: Overweight and weight gain; insulin resistance (International PCOS guideline 2023, Section 3.5).
Family history of PCOS, type 2 diabetes or early cardiovascular disease (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.12.1).

Adolescence, because irregular cycles are common in the first 3 years after menarche, so diagnosis needs both hyperandrogenism and irregular cycles (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendations 1.1.1 and 1.1.3).
Recent combined pill use, which hides androgens and ovulation signs (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.2.6).

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Irregular cycles with low energy, weight gain or galactorrhoea; abnormal thyroid-stimulating hormone or prolactin; always exclude before diagnosing PCOS (clinical judgment; International PCOS guideline 2023, Algorithm 1).
High morning 17-hydroxyprogesterone with hirsutism and irregular cycles; exclude when androgens are markedly raised (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.2.9).
Rapid onset, virilisation, very high testosterone or DHEAS; cortisol excess features (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.2.9).

differentials.condition: Hypothalamic amenorrhoea or premature ovarian insufficiency
differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Low oestrogen with low or very high gonadotrophins, low weight or high training load, no hyperandrogenism (clinical judgment).
Always exclude by pregnancy test in any woman with a missed period (clinical judgment).
Irregular cycles in the first 1 to 3 years after menarche without hyperandrogenism; reassess before diagnosing (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendations 1.1.1, 1.1.3 and 1.1.4).

ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Best used when clinical signs of hyperandrogenism are minimal; unreliable on the combined pill, so repeat after stopping it for 3 months if needed (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendations 1.2.1, 1.2.4 and 1.2.6).
ruleIn.normalValue: Total testosterone about 0.5 to 2.4 nmol/L in women (laboratory dependent)

clinicalManagement.title: Confirm the diagnosis and exclude other causes
actions: Ask about cycle length, hair growth, acne, weight, mood, sleep and family history of diabetes; examine blood pressure, body mass index and hirsutism (modified Ferriman-Gallwey score) (International PCOS guideline 2023, Sections 1.1 and 1.3).
Exclude pregnancy, thyroid disease, high prolactin and non-classical adrenal hyperplasia (International PCOS guideline 2023, Algorithm 1).

Adult with irregular cycles and clinical or biochemical hyperandrogenism: diagnose without ultrasound or anti-Mullerian hormone; otherwise add ultrasound or anti-Mullerian hormone, not both (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendations 1.4.9 and 1.5.5).

Adolescent: need both irregular cycles and hyperandrogenism; if only some features are present record increased risk and review at or before full reproductive maturity (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendations 1.1.3 and 1.1.4).

clinicalManagement.title: Screen for complications
actions: Send a 75 g oral glucose tolerance test, lipid profile and measure blood pressure; repeat glycaemic testing every 1 to 3 years (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendations 1.8.3, 1.8.4 and 1.9.2 to 1.9.3).
Screen all patients for depression and anxiety, and ask about snoring and tiredness for sleep apnoea (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendations 2.2.1, 2.2.2 and 1.10.2).
Ask about eating disorders and body image concerns, with permission to discuss weight and without weight stigma (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendations 2.5.1 and 3.6.2).

clinicalManagement.title: Lifestyle and information
actions: Recommend healthy eating and regular physical activity for all women; no single diet or exercise type is better, so tailor to the woman's preferences (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendations 3.1.1, 3.3.1 and 3.4.1).

Aim at preventing weight gain, with modest weight loss if overweight; aerobic activity in bouts of 10 minutes or more, about 30 minutes on most days (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendations 3.1.2 and 3.4.5).
Use shared decision-making and culturally appropriate education (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendations 2.6.1.1 and 2.6.4.1).

clinicalManagement.title: Treat irregular cycles and hirsutism
clinicalManagement.timeframe: When symptoms trouble the woman and she is not trying to conceive
actions: Offer the combined oral contraceptive pill for irregular cycles and hirsutism in adults, with low-dose ethinylestradiol (20 to 30 micrograms or natural oestrogen) considered (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendations 4.2.1 and 4.2.7).
If the pill is contraindicated or not wanted, use cyclic progestogen for endometrial protection, or metformin for cycles (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendations 4.2.6 and 4.4.5).
For hirsutism not improved after at least 6 months of the pill or cosmetic treatment, add an anti-androgen with effective contraception (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 4.6.1).
Offer laser or light hair removal as an alternative or addition (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 4.8.1).
Inform the woman that untreated amenorrhoea raises endometrial risk, and that regular withdrawal bleeds protect the lining (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendations 1.11.2 and 1.11.4).

clinicalManagement.title: Treat metabolic risk
clinicalManagement.timeframe: When body mass index is 25 or more or glucose is abnormal
actions: Consider metformin for adults with PCOS and body mass index 25 kg/m2 or more; it has efficacy similar to active lifestyle change (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendations 4.3.1 and 4.3.4).
Prefer metformin over the pill for metabolic indications and the pill over metformin for hirsutism with irregular cycles (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendations 4.4.1 and 4.4.2).
Anti-obesity drugs may be added to lifestyle care for higher weight with effective contraception (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendations 4.5.1 and 4.5.2).

clinicalManagement.title: Plan pregnancy and ovulation induction
clinicalManagement.timeframe: When the woman wants to conceive
actions: Optimise weight, blood pressure, smoking, diet, folate (higher dose if body mass index is above 30), sleep and mental health before treatment (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 5.1.2).
Test glucose (oral glucose tolerance test) and measure blood pressure before pregnancy or fertility treatment (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendations 1.9.11 and 4.10.6).
Check semen analysis and consider tubal patency testing before ovulation induction (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 5.2.1).

Use letrozole first; clomiphene or metformin where letrozole is not allowed; gonadotrophins or laparoscopic ovarian surgery in clomiphene resistance, at a fertility service (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendations 5.3.1, 5.4.5.1 and 5.5.4).

Exclude pregnancy before every cycle; clomiphene needs ultrasound monitoring because of multiple pregnancy (International PCOS guideline 2023, Section 5 general principles and Recommendation 5.4.2.2).
Flag PCOS in antenatal care; offer glucose testing at the first antenatal visit and at 24 to 28 weeks (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendations 4.10.1 and 4.10.7).

regimens.indication: Irregular cycles and hirsutism in PCOS (off-label for PCOS; label is contraception)
regimens.patientGroup: Adult women with PCOS not trying to conceive
regimens.dose: One pink active tablet (levonorgestrel 0.15 mg with ethinylestradiol 30 micrograms) once daily for 21 days, then one white inactive tablet daily for 7 days, then start the next pack. Dilution and preparation: none; oral tablet, no crushing or reconstitution unless stated.
regimens.route: Oral, at the same time every day with or without food; start on day 1 of the period, or the first Sunday after it with condoms for the first 7 days (Portia label, Dosage and Administration)
regimens.duration: Continue while symptoms need control and no contraindication develops; review yearly
adjustments: Ethinylestradiol 20 to 30 micrograms or natural oestrogen is suggested; no preference between products is set by the guideline (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendations 4.2.3, 4.2.4 and 4.2.7).
The 35 microgram ethinylestradiol with cyproterone acetate pill is second line because of venous thromboembolism risk (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 4.2.5).
Androgen blood tests are unreliable while on the pill (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.2.6).
Enzyme inducers (carbamazepine, phenytoin, rifampicin, efavirenz, St. John's wort) reduce contraceptive effect; use a backup method (Portia label, Drug interactions).
Exclude pregnancy before starting (pregnancy test).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register returned an empty page from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Blood pressure, weight and bleeding pattern at 3 months, then yearly.
Signs of thrombosis: leg swelling, chest pain, breathlessness, severe headache or visual loss (Portia label, Warnings 1).
contraindications: Smoker over 35 years (boxed warning); current or past deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism; cerebrovascular disease; coronary artery disease (Portia label, Contraindications).
Thrombogenic valve or rhythm disease; inherited or acquired clotting disorder (Portia label, Contraindications).
Uncontrolled hypertension or hypertension with vascular disease; diabetes over age 35 or with vascular disease, end-organ damage or duration over 20 years (Portia label, Contraindications).
Migraine with aura, headaches with focal neurological symptoms, or any migraine over age 35 (Portia label, Contraindications).

Breast cancer; liver tumour, acute viral hepatitis or decompensated cirrhosis; undiagnosed abnormal uterine bleeding; ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir hepatitis C regimens (Portia label, Contraindications).

regimens.indication: Secondary amenorrhoea or irregular bleeding from hormonal imbalance in PCOS; protects the endometrium (label indication: secondary amenorrhoea and abnormal uterine bleeding)
regimens.patientGroup: Adult women with PCOS not trying to conceive and with a negative pregnancy test
regimens.dose: 10 mg once daily for 10 days (5 mg to 10 mg daily for 5 to 10 days is the labelled range). Dilution and preparation: none; oral tablet, no crushing or reconstitution unless stated.
regimens.route: Oral, once daily at the same time each day (medroxyprogesterone label, Dosage and Administration)
regimens.frequency: Once daily for the course; planned cycles repeated at an interval chosen by the prescriber
regimens.duration: 5 to 10 days per course; progestin withdrawal bleeding usually follows 3 to 7 days after the last tablet
adjustments: Interval between courses is not set by the guideline; regular progestogen is advised for endometrial protection (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.11.4).
It is not a contraceptive; offer contraception if pregnancy is not wanted.
Progestin-only oral contraceptives may also be used for endometrial protection (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 4.2.6).
Exclude pregnancy before starting (pregnancy test).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register returned an empty page from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Bleeding pattern after each course; if no withdrawal bleed repeat pregnancy test and review.
Blood pressure and signs of thrombosis.
contraindications: Undiagnosed abnormal genital bleeding; known or suspected pregnancy (medroxyprogesterone label, Contraindications).
Known, suspected or past breast cancer or oestrogen- or progesterone-dependent neoplasia (medroxyprogesterone label, Contraindications).
Active or past deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism; active or past arterial thromboembolic disease such as stroke or myocardial infarction (medroxyprogesterone label, Contraindications).
Known liver impairment or disease; anaphylaxis or angioedema to medroxyprogesterone (medroxyprogesterone label, Contraindications).

regimens.indication: Hirsutism not improved after at least 6 months of the combined pill or cosmetic therapy (off-label)
regimens.patientGroup: Adult women with PCOS and persistent hirsutism, on effective contraception
regimens.dose: 25 mg to 100 mg once daily (guideline range); start at 25 mg and increase as tolerated. Dilution and preparation: none; oral tablet, no crushing or reconstitution unless stated.
regimens.route: Oral, with or without food but taken consistently in relation to food (spironolactone label, Section 2.1)
regimens.duration: Review response at 6 months; continue while hirsutism needs control
adjustments: Always combine with effective contraception (intrauterine device or combined pill) because anti-androgens can cause incomplete development of external genitalia in a male fetus (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendations 4.6.3 and 4.6.4).
Renal: hyperkalaemia risk rises with reduced kidney function; eGFR 30 to 50 mL/min/1.73 m2 needs a lower start (spironolactone label, Section 2.2).
Cyproterone acetate 10 mg or more, finasteride, flutamide and bicalutamide carry higher risks (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 4.6.5).
Exclude pregnancy before starting (pregnancy test).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register returned an empty page from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Serum potassium within 1 week of starting or increasing the dose and regularly afterwards (spironolactone label, Section 5.1).
Blood pressure and menstrual irregularity; hirsutism score at 6 months.
contraindications: Hyperkalaemia; Addison's disease; concomitant use of eplerenone (spironolactone label, Section 4).
Pregnancy or a woman not using effective contraception (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 4.6.3).

regimens.indication: Metabolic risk in PCOS with body mass index 25 kg/m2 or more, and irregular cycles when the pill cannot be used (off-label for PCOS; label is type 2 diabetes)
regimens.dose: Start 500 mg once or twice daily with meals and increase by 500 mg every 1 to 2 weeks as tolerated; the guideline suggests a maximum of 2.5 g a day in adults (label maximum 2,550 mg a day in divided doses). Extended-release tablets start at 500 mg with the evening meal and may reduce stomach side effects. Dilution and preparation: none; oral tablet, no crushing or reconstitution unless stated.
regimens.route: Oral with meals; swallow extended-release tablets whole and never crush, cut or chew (metformin label, Section 2.1)
regimens.frequency: Once to three times daily with meals
regimens.duration: Long-term; review the need for ongoing treatment regularly
adjustments: Renal: contraindicated if eGFR is below 30 mL/min/1.73 m2; do not start if eGFR is 30 to 45; reassess if eGFR falls below 45 (metformin label, Section 2.3).
Stop before iodinated contrast imaging if eGFR is 30 to 60 or with liver disease, alcoholism or heart failure; recheck eGFR after 48 hours (metformin label, Section 2.4).
Low vitamin B12 can occur; consider monitoring in women with risk factors (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 4.3.4).
Pregnancy: not shown to prevent gestational diabetes or pre-eclampsia (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 4.11.1).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register returned an empty page from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: eGFR before starting and at least yearly; vitamin B12 if risk factors.
Gastrointestinal side effects; warn about lactic acidosis symptoms: malaise, muscle pain, abdominal pain, fast breathing (metformin label, Section 5.1).
contraindications: Severe renal impairment (eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73 m2); hypersensitivity to metformin (metformin label, Section 4).
Acute or chronic metabolic acidosis including diabetic ketoacidosis (metformin label, Section 4).

regimens.indication: Ovulation induction in infertile anovulatory women with PCOS and no other infertility factor (off-label; label is breast cancer)
regimens.patientGroup: Women with PCOS who want to conceive
regimens.dose: 2.5 mg once daily for 5 days starting on cycle day 3; the dose used in the cited trial was 2.5 mg or 5 mg on cycle days 3 to 7. Dilution and preparation: none; oral tablet, no crushing or reconstitution unless stated.
regimens.route: Oral, once daily without regard to meals (letrozole label, Section 2.1)
regimens.frequency: Once daily for 5 days each cycle
regimens.duration: One to three cycles in the trial; the guideline sets no limit, so review at a fertility service
adjustments: Hepatic: cirrhosis with severe dysfunction needs a 50% lower dose (letrozole label, Section 2.5).
Not given if any chance of pre-existing pregnancy; no evidence of more malformations than clomiphene or natural conception (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendations 5.3.3 and 5.4.5.2).
Start folic acid preconception care and exclude pregnancy before each cycle (International PCOS guideline 2023, Section 5 general principles).
Letrozole may reduce bone density with long use (letrozole label, Section 5.1).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register returned an empty page from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Pregnancy test before each cycle; ovulation and follicle monitoring as the fertility service advises.
Multiple pregnancy risk is lower than with clomiphene but ultrasound monitoring is still used in many centres.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to letrozole or any excipient (letrozole label, Section 4).

regimens.indication: Ovulatory dysfunction in women desiring pregnancy; PCOS is a labelled responsive group
regimens.patientGroup: Women with PCOS who want to conceive
regimens.dose: 50 mg once daily for 5 days; if ovulation does not occur, 100 mg once daily for 5 days in the next course, started no earlier than 30 days after the previous course; do not exceed 100 mg a day for 5 days. Dilution and preparation: none; oral tablet, no crushing or reconstitution unless stated.
regimens.route: Oral, once daily; start about day 5 of the cycle after a progestin-induced or spontaneous bleed, or at any time if there has been no recent bleed (clomiphene label, Dosage and Administration)
regimens.frequency: Once daily for 5 days each cycle
regimens.duration: Up to 3 courses without ovulation, then reassess; no more than about 6 cycles in total (clomiphene label)
adjustments: Use the low 50 mg dose in PCOS because of ovarian hyperstimulation risk (clomiphene label, Dosage and Administration).
Add metformin to improve ovulation and pregnancy rates, with monitoring as for clomiphene alone (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendations 5.4.3.1 and 5.4.4.2).
Multiple pregnancy is increased; arrange ultrasound monitoring (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 5.4.2.2).
Examine for ovarian enlargement or cysts before each course (clomiphene label).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register returned an empty page from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Pregnancy test and pelvic examination or ultrasound before each course for ovarian enlargement.
Visual symptoms (blurring, spots, flashes): stop and review (clomiphene label, Precautions).
contraindications: Pregnancy; hypersensitivity to clomiphene (clomiphene label, Contraindications).
Liver disease or history of liver dysfunction (clomiphene label, Contraindications).
Abnormal uterine bleeding of undetermined origin (clomiphene label, Contraindications).
Ovarian cysts or enlargement not caused by PCOS (clomiphene label, Indications and Usage).

medicationPlan.note: Drug classes and indications follow the 2023 International Evidence-based PCOS Guideline; doses, dilution, administration and contraindications come from the product labels named in each row (US prescribing information). The letrozole start dose is from a published trial. All doses are for adults. Medical therapy is generally not approved specifically for PCOS, so use is evidence-based but off-label; explain the evidence and side effects (International PCOS guideline 2023, Section 4.1). SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register returned an empty page from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Two of three after other causes are excluded: clinical or biochemical hyperandrogenism; irregular cycles (ovulatory dysfunction); polycystic ovarian morphology on ultrasound, or serum anti-Mullerian hormone instead of ultrasound (International PCOS guideline 2023, Discussion and Algorithm 1).
Irregular cycles plus hyperandrogenism is enough; ultrasound or anti-Mullerian hormone is not needed (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.4.9 and 1.5.2).
Both irregular cycles and hyperandrogenism; do not use ultrasound or anti-Mullerian hormone (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.4.6 and 1.5.4).

Follicle number per ovary 20 or more in at least one ovary; or ovarian volume 10 mL or more, or follicle number per section 10 or more with older equipment (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendations 1.4.4 and 1.4.5).

75 g oral glucose tolerance test at diagnosis and every 1 to 3 years; also before pregnancy, at the first antenatal visit and at 24 to 28 weeks (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendations 1.9.2, 1.9.3, 1.9.9 and 1.9.11).

Lipid profile at diagnosis; blood pressure yearly and before pregnancy; screen for sleep apnoea symptoms, depression and anxiety (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendations 1.8.3, 1.8.4, 1.10.2, 2.2.1 and 2.2.2).

Anovulatory infertility with no other fertility factor; letrozole first line; exclude pregnancy; start preconception care (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 5.3.1 and Section 5 general principles).

teaching.scope: Woman or adolescent in primary care, a gynaecology or an endocrine clinic in Saudi Arabia with suspected or confirmed polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS): diagnosis by the 2023 international guideline criteria, screening for glucose, lipid, blood pressure, sleep and mood problems, lifestyle care, management of irregular cycles and hirsutism, metabolic treatment with metformin, ovulation induction and pregnancy planning. Uses the 2023 International Evidence-based Guideline (the Saudi-relevant prevalence comes from a 2026 Gulf Cooperation Council meta-analysis), with doses, dilution, administration and contraindications taken from product labels.
learningObjectives: Diagnose PCOS correctly in adults and adolescents and exclude other causes.
Screen every woman for glucose, lipid, blood pressure, sleep and mood problems.
Choose the right treatment for cycles, hirsutism, metabolic risk and infertility.
Plan pregnancy and flag PCOS in antenatal care.
pitfalls: Diagnosing PCOS from one irregular cycle in a girl less than 3 years after menarche.
Skipping the 75 g glucose test because the woman is not overweight.
Starting letrozole, clomiphene or spironolactone before a pregnancy test.
Using a combined pill in a woman with migraine with aura or smoking over 35.
Using weight-loss advice alone without addressing mood, hirsutism and fertility goals.
keyPoints: Do not use ultrasound or anti-Mullerian hormone to diagnose PCOS in adolescents.
Letrozole is the first-line ovulation induction drug but is off-label in many countries.
Anti-androgens must be given with effective contraception.
A normal weight does not remove the metabolic and cardiovascular risk.
Androgen results are unreliable on the combined pill.

patientEducation: PCOS is a lifelong but manageable condition; periods, hair growth and fertility can all be treated.
Healthy eating and regular activity help every woman with PCOS, even without weight loss.
Take hormone tablets exactly as prescribed; report leg swelling, chest pain or sudden breathlessness at once.
You must use effective contraception while taking spironolactone and tell us at once if you may be pregnant.
Mood changes, low confidence and tiredness are common; tell us so we can help.
lifestyleAndDiet: Follow a balanced diet that suits your preferences; no one diet is best.
Aim for activity in bouts of at least 10 minutes, about 30 minutes on most days.
Avoid smoking, especially if you take the combined pill.
Seek help for snoring with daytime sleepiness.
mdtReferrals: Primary care physician; gynaecologist; endocrinologist; fertility specialist; dietitian; psychologist or psychiatrist; dermatologist for laser hair removal; sleep clinic.
dischargeCriteria: Diagnosis recorded with the criteria used; glucose, lipid, blood pressure, mood and sleep screens done; a treatment plan agreed for cycles, hair, weight and fertility; contraception or pregnancy plan documented; follow-up booked.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Review at 3 months after any new drug, then at least yearly: weight, blood pressure, cycle pattern, hirsutism, mood and sleep; glucose testing every 1 to 3 years and earlier before pregnancy; lipids as risk dictates; fertility review after 3 to 6 ovulatory cycles without pregnancy; antenatal flagging of PCOS when pregnant.
